Resolves #20350

Re-enabling selection on an ordinary checkbox list now restores its checked records into the selection model and restores their existing item annotations. The first click unchecks its record again. Initial item creation and re-enabling share the same event-free seeding helper; single-select retains the first checked record in current store order without rewriting the other record flags.

Evidence: L2 (single-thread Node tests with real List, Store and selection-model instances) → L2 required (both acceptance criteria are unit-level record/model/VDOM observations). Residual: none for the stated ordinary-list criteria.

Class: restoration (`fix`). agent-preflight: not hosted here (npm reports Missing script); shared baseline checks run on the PR.
Micro-review eligible: contained — restores the existing checked-field contract through the existing annotation owner.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `UseCheckBoxes.spec.mjs` — reset and no-reset first-click controls, immediate record/model/VDOM state, retained item identity, no record changes or extra selection events during re-enable. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the filtered custom-field single-select arm retains all record flags and checked annotations while selecting only the first visible record in descending store order. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. `seedCheckedSelection(restore)` extracts the existing `createItems()` loop and optionally delegates annotation restoration to `selection.Model#restoreSelection()`. Buffered/tree lists and ValuePicker remain outside this leaf's certification.

## Test Evidence

Red-first control on unchanged source: the re-enable multi-select and filtered single-select arms failed with empty model selection; the no-reset control and existing arms passed. After the repair, both regression arms pass. Routine coverage runs in CI.

## Post-Merge Validation

No additional merge-only acceptance step. The tests assert existing VDOM annotations; they do not claim a native-browser paint receipt.
